verdict.rationale: The product has a public GitHub repository. Its README includes a monorepo development command (`pnpm --filter @omnirush/desktop dev`), which implies the desktop app's source can be read and run locally. However, nothing in the evidence names a license, so the 'open license' half of the story is unproven. missing for 10: an explicit open-source license (e.g., a LICENSE file or license statement), confirmation that the full app source rather than just build tooling is published, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: omnirush.ai is a desktop app for working with a coding agent on your own projects.
